channel.title: Text Preparation Journal
channel.description: Field notes on cleaning, structuring, and preparing text before it enters another system.

item.title: A Prepared Handoff Is Not an Accepted Outcome
item.description: PasteLint reports the preparation it can observe without implying publication, deployment, delivery, or downstream acceptance.

item.title: Text Readiness Is a Handoff Discipline
item.description: Good writing is only part of successful communication. Every destination requires deliberate preparation, and every handoff deserves editorial care.

item.title: Editors Optimize for Readers. Humanizers Optimize for Detectors.
item.description: Three cases show why editorial preparation and detector optimization are different objectives: one improves communication; the other pursues a classifier score.

item.title: The Record Behind Product Transparency
item.description: Why durable reasoning, evidence, tradeoffs, corrections, and limits reveal more than release notes or announcements alone.

item.title: A Tutor Prompt Is More Than a Refusal
item.description: A student-designed prompt replaces assignment-ready prose with explanation, questions, and another attempt. Research supports parts of that learning loop—but not universal refusal, guaranteed learning, or a new requirement for writing tools.

item.title: Line Breaks Are Part of the Meaning
item.description: An earlier version of SecondDraft preserved every word in a five-line message while collapsing its structure. The repaired engine now leaves those line boundaries intact.

item.title: Clearer Is Not More Certain
item.description: Removing a hedge can make a sentence cleaner while changing what it claims. Learn how to preserve uncertainty, judgment, and recommendation strength.

item.title: Directness Without False Certainty
item.description: Why SecondDraft stopped treating qualified language as something to delete.

item.title: The First Draft Finds the Story. Revision Makes It Work.
item.description: Three experienced screenwriters approach rewriting from complementary angles: discovering what the script became, repairing how it begins, and allowing the story to evolve when it meets production reality.

item.title: The New Bottleneck Isn’t Code—It’s Taste
item.description: A practitioner built a functional AI-assisted application, then confronted the harder problem: making it feel considered rather than generated. The case suggests that as construction becomes easier, hierarchy, restraint, and design judgment become more valuable.

item.title: Filler Openings Make AI Drafts Feel Unfinished
item.description: An Editor's Desk note on why filler openings weaken generated copy and how cleaner revision starts by finding the real sentence underneath.

item.title: Preserving Catalog Records Across SSML Chunks
item.description: An Engine Room note on improving SSML Builder chunking so catalog titles, DB numbers, authors, narrators, and descriptions stay together when possible.

item.title: Tracing Changes the Conditions Around the Output
item.description: A Text Preparation Journal source note on completion-oriented prompting, collapse prevention, and why text preparation begins before the next response is generated.

item.title: The Cleanup Pass Is Where Voice Survives
item.description: A Text Preparation Journal note on why AI-assisted revision should make edits visible, reviewable, and owned by the writer.

item.title: The Content Pipeline Breaks Before the Writing Does
item.description: A Text Preparation Journal note on how one r/micro_saas SEO post reveals the workflow problem behind content consistency, cleanup, and publishing readiness.
